target: चाय में अदरक का एक टुकड़ा डालो।
english: Add a piece of ginger to the tea.
reason: Niche recipe step with the bookish word मिश्रण; no home cook says दही और बेसन का मिश्रण डालो. Replacement keeps में + का + imperative डालो in an everyday kitchen sentence.

target: पहले हमारे घर के पास एक छोटी दुकान होती थी।
english: Earlier there used to be a small shop near our house.
reason: Encyclopedic trivia about telephone history, and कम घरों में without बहुत reads stilted. Replacement keeps the habitual past होता था pattern in a sentence someone would actually say.

target: शाम को लोग पार्क में बैठकर बातें करते हैं।
english: In the evening people sit in the park and chat.
reason: Encyclopedic festival trivia (Lohri bonfires) written as a third-person description a learner will never use. Replacement keeps -कर + habitual present with everyday vocabulary.

target: मेरा भाई एक दुकान में काम करता है।
english: My brother works in a shop.
reason: Decorative occupation card (potter making earthen pots); pure textbook filler, not usable speech. Replacement keeps the same simple-present third-person structure.

target: इतनी दूर पैदल जाने का कोई फ़ायदा नहीं है।
english: There is no point in walking that far.
reason: Preachy motto about the joys of the joint family, not something a person says in conversation. Replacement keeps the oblique infinitive + का ... है structure.

target: बच्चे गाना गाते हुए स्कूल जा रहे थे।
english: The children were going to school singing.
reason: Parade scene (marching in step while drumming) is decorative and unusable. Replacement keeps the -ते हुए participle with past continuous.

target: पहले खाना खा लो, फिर बाहर जाना।
reason: Proverb / moralising maxim (think before you speak). Replacement keeps the two-clause imperative pattern in ordinary household speech.

target: मैंने दाल चखकर देखी, नमक थोड़ा कम है।
english: I tasted the dal; the salt is a bit less.
reason: Subjectless and stilted; नमक जाँचा is not how anyone says it. Replacement keeps the -कर conjunctive participle in natural kitchen speech.

target: कमरे के अंदर कोई सो रहा है।
english: Someone is sleeping inside the room.
reason: दरवाज़े के अंदर does not mean in the doorway; a speaker would say दरवाज़े पर. Replacement keeps the के अंदर compound postposition where it actually fits.

english: The shopkeeper opened the shop in the morning.
reason: खटीक is an obscure caste-linked term for butcher that a learner will never need. Replacement keeps the ने + object + perfective structure with common vocabulary.

target: पहले मैं इसी दुकान से सब्ज़ी लेता था।
english: I used to buy vegetables from this same shop.
reason: Decorative village vignette (an old barber sitting at the square); nothing a learner can reuse. Replacement keeps the habitual past लेता था.

target: हम रोज़ सुबह उठकर टहलने जाते थे।
english: We used to get up early every morning and go for a walk.
reason: Village well-and-rope nostalgia, irrelevant to everyday speech. Replacement keeps -कर plus habitual past in a sentence about ordinary routine.

target: शाम को बाज़ार में बहुत भीड़ होती थी।
english: The market used to be very crowded in the evening.
reason: Literary and decorative (चौपाल गुलज़ार होता था); गुलज़ार is ornamental vocabulary. Replacement keeps the habitual past होती थी with common words.

target: पहले हमारे घर में रोज़ शाम को चाय बनाई जाती थी।
english: Tea used to be made at our home every evening.
reason: Same village-chaupal nostalgia stratum, pure atmosphere rather than usable language. Replacement keeps the habitual past passive (बनाई जाती थी).
